blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — treatment of mild hypoglycemia
stem: An alert client with diabetes who can swallow has a blood glucose of 62 mg/dL and reports shakiness. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Give 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate, then recheck the glucose in 15 minutes and repeat treatment if hypoglycemia persists.
options.B: Administer intravenous dextrose immediately even though the client is alert, able to swallow, and able to take oral carbohydrate safely.
options.C: Give the client's scheduled rapid-acting insulin dose, then recheck the glucose in 15 minutes to determine whether symptoms improve.
options.D: Delay carbohydrate treatment until the next meal because a glucose value above 54 mg/dL does not require immediate intervention.

rationale: The American Diabetes Association Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 recommend treating hypoglycemia at 70 mg/dL or less with fast-acting carbohydrate in a person who is alert and able to take oral carbohydrate. For most individuals, 15 g of carbohydrate is used; glucose is rechecked 15 minutes later and treatment is repeated if hypoglycemia persists. Therefore A is correct. IV glucose or glucagon is reserved for situations in which oral carbohydrate cannot be taken safely or effectively, insulin would worsen the hypoglycemia, and delaying treatment is inconsistent with the recommended threshold.
educational_objective: Treat hypoglycemia in an alert client who can swallow with 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate, recheck glucose in 15 minutes, and repeat treatment if hypoglycemia persists.
source_document_title: 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_version_date: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl. 1), January 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Hypoglycemia Treatment section: treat at glucose 70 mg/dL or less with fast-acting carbohydrate; for most individuals 15 g; recheck glucose after 15 minutes and repeat if hypoglycemia persists.
source_claim_supported: For an alert person able to take oral carbohydrate, hypoglycemia at 70 mg/dL or less should be treated with fast-acting carbohydrate; for most individuals 15 g is used, with glucose rechecked after 15 minutes and treatment repeated if hypoglycemia persists.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: evaluate client response to medication; educate client about medications; administer medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as realistic immediate treatment decisions of comparable length.
Preserved the current ADA 15-g/15-minute recommendation for a generic alert client who can swallow while excluding IV treatment, insulin, and delay as second answers.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A is uniquely appropriate for this alert, swallowing-capable client with glucose 62 mg/dL. The stem does not identify an automated-insulin-delivery exception, and B–D are clinically inappropriate alternatives rather than second defensible answers.
